low_energy_kernel_validation.protocol: rho=1e-2,1e-3,1e-4 with rho*theta fixed at .5,1,2, three directions and two valleys; all 17 candidates without detected gapped zero witnesses, including uniform B control
low_energy_kernel_validation.conclusion: The full local projector approaches the derived Dirac-boundary kernel linearly in rho on every tested group. This validates a local scaling limit, not finite-theta entropy scaling.
low_energy_kernel_validation.two_dimensional_formula_note: The roughly 1e-8 error for uniform A/B arises from square-root sensitivity to roundoff in |n_z|=1; all nonuniform two-dimensional checks agree to roundoff.

derivations.gapped_graph: A=V_minus^dagger P, B=V_plus^dagger P. Where A is invertible, X(theta)=exp(-theta E_plus) B inv(A) exp(theta E_minus). The norm bound exp(-Delta*theta)*sqrt(s_min^-2-1) exposes an initial-state-dependent prefactor. A uniform positive lower bound on s away from Dirac nodes gives a uniform microscopic projection time on that compact momentum region.
derivations.uniform: For uniform A/B, every negative-band overlap is exactly 1/sqrt(2). In an unfolded 2x2 block, C_theta=[I-tanh(2*epsilon*theta)H/epsilon +/-sech(2*epsilon*theta)sigma_z]/2. The only critical crossover variable is epsilon*theta; epsilon~v|q-K| gives the ordinary theta length scale. No extra gapped zero-overlap layer exists.
derivations.minor: For chiral H=[0,T;T^dagger,0], polar unitary U=T(T^dagger T)^-1/2 gives V_minus=[I;-U^dagger]/sqrt(2). At half filling, the overlap determinant reduces, up to a nonzero factor and sign, to the minor of U linking occupied B sites to empty A sites. Thus the spatial arrangement, not only A/B counts, controls extra zeros.
derivations.dirac: If gap~v*r and the relevant overlap behaves as r^p, the graph bound contains r^-p exp(-v*r*theta). This can add logarithmic overlap costs to projection times compared with a bounded Dirac boundary overlap. It does not by itself determine D or prove a log-log entropy correction.
derivations.effective_boundary: At an exact folded Dirac momentum, remove the filled high-negative directions: R spans ker(V_high_negative^dagger P). The low-energy initial boundary is Q_b=orth(V_zero^dagger P R), provided the high-negative rank and zero-support rank are correct. Evolving Q_b with the projected linear Dirac Hamiltonian describes the rho->0, theta->infinity, rho*theta fixed local kernel. The script tests this limit against the full analytic Bloch evolution; it does not compute entropy.
derivations.boundary_mass: M=2 Q_b Q_b^dagger-I is a flattened initial-boundary matrix, not an added physical Hamiltonian term. For uniform A/B it anticommutes with both Dirac kinetic matrices. More general regular boundaries need not anticommute. In a two-dimensional zero space with sublattice polarization n_z, the smallest negative-Dirac overlap over all directions is sqrt((1-sqrt(1-n_z^2))/2); n_z=0 is the angular-obstruction case. Four-dimensional valley-mixed zero spaces require the full angular matrix test.
derivations.valley_folding_symmetry: The primitive Dirac valleys K_plus/minus=(+/-2pi/3,+/-2pi/3) fold to the same m-by-m supercell momentum exactly when m is divisible by 3. Otherwise primitive translation by the supercell separates the two two-dimensional valley blocks. For m divisible by 3, a periodic initial configuration can mix the valleys in a four-dimensional zero space; its mean sublattice polarization is not a sufficient boundary-regularity criterion.
derivations.conditional_scaling_argument: If overlaps away from Dirac points have a uniform positive lower bound and the effective Dirac boundary is nondegenerate in every direction, then there is no extra divergent gapped projection scale, and the low-energy kernel depends on rho*theta after a finite initial-state crossover. Modes at separations a<<r<<v*theta can then approach the GS critical kernel; obtaining the same corner-log coefficient is the natural scaling argument. This is conditional physical reasoning, not a rigorous theorem for the full Renyi entropy or proof from a finite grid.

interpretation: The two shifted momentum grids and local minimizers do not prove absence of continuum zeros. Values below 1e-8 at a gapped point are numerical zero witnesses, not exact symbolic theorems.
A finite-size ground-reachability audit may miss a continuum zero at an incommensurate momentum. A near-zero also produces large but finite crossover time without any true zero.
The derivative Jacobian tests local first-order complex overlap structure only. It does not alone certify a global zero line or a topological defect.
Dirac angular/radial scans are candidate diagnostics. Avoid labeling an overlap minimum caused by the physical vanishing energy gap as an extra gapped obstruction.

A concrete finite-sampling caution: the 48-direction full-overlap scan misses angular zeros of some blocked m2 stripes, while the effective-boundary angular minimizer finds them. A nonzero sampled minimum must never be promoted to a continuum theorem.
All conclusions concern beta=0 before measurement. No entropy is computed, and no pattern is declared to have a certified GS corner coefficient from this scan alone.
Uniform A/B is the safest analytic reference. Other patterns can only be prioritized for actual size-plateau and time-window tests after these spectral diagnostics.

primary_reference.scope: The paper proposes a finite-size scaling ansatz and motivates its short-time limit by xi~tau^(1/z). Its free-fermion experiment starts from an AFM product state and checks size-independent plateaus. It is not a proof of this single-scale condition for arbitrary periodic product configurations.
